title: When fungi knock, nitrilases unlock the auxin arsenal
content: Botrytis cinerea, the causal agent of gray mold, is a devastating necrotrophic pathogen that infects more than 1,400 plant species and causes substantial agricultural losses globally (Elad et al. 2015). Plants perceive fungal chitin through cell surface–localized pattern-recognition receptors such as CHITIN ELICITOR RECEPTOR KINASE 1 (CERK1) to initiate pattern-triggered immunity (PTI) (Yang et al. 2022). While plant hormones, such as auxin, are known to bolster defense responses against B. cinerea (Llorente et al. 2008), a fundamental question has remained: how do plants rapidly activate auxin biosynthesis upon pathogen attack, and what molecular mechanism links chitin-triggered CERK1 signaling to the auxin pathway? Reporting in new work, Jiarui Zheng and colleagues (Zheng et al. 2026) revealed that CERK1 directly phosphorylates nitrilases to promote indole-3-acetonitrile (IAN)-dependent auxin biosynthesis, thereby strengthening host resistance against gray mold.
